final_text:
The data can't say which organism caused the sepsis, so I'm calling it `cannot_determine`.

The top three non-human species by clade reads are:
- *Cutibacterium acnes* (524 reads), a common skin organism. Its genus is not in the contaminant list. The list has *Propionibacterium*, its older name, but a plain match on the current name doesn't flag it.
- *Acidovorax* sp. JMULE5 (331 reads), whose genus is on the reagent contaminant list.
- *Staphylococcus epidermidis* (182 reads), a skin commensal. Its genus is not on the contaminant list.

All three are typical skin flora or reagent contaminants, and the counts are tiny. Most of the 500,000 read pairs are unclassified or human, and no organism stands out. No lab confirmation is available, so I can't tell a causative pathogen from background.

I counted only entries at the species rank (S). *Brevundimonas* is large at genus level (1,473 reads) but has no species entry above 23 reads, so it doesn't make the top three.
